body:
## Confirmed production defect

MediaDive `get_compounds_of_solution()` keyed recipe entries by cleaned display name. A repeated name silently overwrote an earlier occurrence and its quantities. The production emitter consumed that lossy dictionary and also accumulated ingredient declarations across solutions by name.

Pinned local `data/raw/mediadive/solutions.json` SHA256: `9ab0fbf72c2e5ac25ecab3ada268dfe524db971daa86d67532dea6a5412a5c44`.

Concrete solution `5787`, compound `981`, label `NiCl2 x 2 H2O`:

- raw list position / recipe_order 2: amount `284`, unit `mg`, `g_l=0.284`, `mmol_l=2.19138`;
- raw list position / recipe_order 4: amount `166`, unit `mg`, `g_l=0.166`, `mmol_l=1.28087`.

The old dictionary retained only the second row. The complete source inventory finds 80 duplicate-name groups in 71 solutions, 161 involved occurrences and 81 overwritten occurrences; 58 groups have differing quantities. Counts describe this fingerprinted input, not freshly transformed graph totals.

## Required correction

Preserve source occurrences in ordered records with the original raw recipe item and stable owning-solution/list-position assertion identity. Emit each occurrence independently, including equal-target/equal-quantity repeats. Keep amount, unit, mass concentration, molar concentration, raw source IDs, original names and supplied order paired correctly. Do not sum, invent display-label suffixes, infer typo corrections, or merge distinct source observations.

Retain the existing unique-name convenience API only if collisions fail explicitly, and keep production emission on the lossless API. Accumulate endpoint nodes by resolved ID plus display label, not by display name alone. Test the actual writer, source finalization and KGX archive round trip offline with immutable raw excerpts and synthetic adversarial collisions.
title: Preserve every MediaDive recipe occurrence and quantity through transform and merge
